introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography (0750), Paper 3, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Duration: three and a quarter hours.**

Answer FOUR questions in all. Answer question ONE and three others, choosing at least ONE question from SECTION B and TWO from SECTION C. Question ONE carries thirty-one marks and the rest carry twenty-three marks each.

Only the required number of questions will be marked.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references.

Candidates are advised NOT to attempt the questions on field investigations if such an exercise has not been carried out.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed.

Materials required: Topographic map, graph paper and two outline maps of Cameroon.

Les faits cités (régions, institutions, sites) sont ceux de la géographie du Cameroun couramment enseignée ; les chiffres sont arrondis et donnés avec « about » quand ils ne sont pas certains ; aucune statistique précise n'est avancée. À relire par un géographe avant mise en avant.

Les faits cités sont à vérifier avant mise en avant : noms d'institutions et de sites (par exemple Wakwa, Jakiri, Waza, Korup, Campo-Ma'an, Dja, Lobeke, SODECOTON, CICAM), séries chronologiques (insécurité du Nord depuis environ 2013-2014, abattage d'éléphants vers 2012) et ordres de grandeur ; tout chiffre précis a été omis ou donné avec « about ».

Question 7(a) : la description des sols du Plateau de l'Adamaoua (ferrallitiques sur socle, volcaniques sur basalte, lithosols, hydromorphes) est la classification couramment enseignée ; aucun pourcentage n'est donné. Question 7(b) : le sujet imprime « (6, 4 marks) » pour b) (i) et (ii) : 10 points pour le bloc. Points imprimés : 6 + 10 + 7 = 23.

questions.enonce_markdown: 7. a) Describe the soil characteristics of the Adamawa Plateau. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Main soil types and their characteristics (6 marks).**

- **Ferrallitic (red and yellow) soils**, the dominant type, formed on granite and gneiss under the savanna climate with a long wet season: **deep**, strongly weathered and leached, **acidic**, with a high content of iron and aluminium oxides (red to yellow-brown colour), a sandy-clay or clay-loam texture, a **low natural fertility** (few nutrients, poor in phosphorus and humus) but a good, porous structure.
- **Volcanic soils on the basalt** (for example in the Ngaoundere area): dark red-brown or dark soils, richer in nutrients and clay, more fertile, which support better pastures and crops.
- **Shallow, stony soils (lithosols)** on steep slopes, scarps and around the inselbergs, with a thin profile, gravelly texture and rock outcrops; they are thin and easily eroded.
- **Hydromorphic and alluvial soils** in the valley bottoms and along the streams: dark, waterlogged in the rainy season, richer in humus and used for dry-season gardens.
- **Laterite (ironstone) crusts** are found in places where the iron-rich layer hardens when exposed.
- **General features**: low organic matter because of bush fires and grazing, a fairly thin humus layer, sensitivity to **erosion and gullying** when the grass is overgrazed, and the leaching of nutrients by the heavy rains.

*Marks: any three types or characteristics, each described (about 2 marks).*

questions.enonce_markdown:
b) i) Examine any TWO push factors of inter-regional migration trends in Cameroon.

ii) Explain TWO efforts to redress the trends. (6, 4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(b)(i) Two push factors (6 marks, 3 each).**

1. **Poor and unreliable agricultural conditions / land degradation**: in the Far North and North, drought, the shrinking of Lake Chad, soil exhaustion and floods push farmers and herders south to the Adamawa, the Centre and the Littoral; in the over-populated Western Highlands, the land shortage and the fragmentation of farms push people towards the plantation and forest areas and towards Douala and Yaounde.
2. **Unemployment, poverty and the lack of social amenities and infrastructure**: schools, hospitals, electricity, water and roads, and paid jobs, are lacking in the rural regions, so young people leave for the big cities and for the regions with plantations and mines.
3. **Insecurity and conflict**: attacks by armed groups in the Far North and the crisis in the North-West and South-West Regions force people to leave their homes, an important recent push factor.

*(Any two; each push factor described with an example.)*

**(b)(ii) Two efforts to redress the trends (4 marks, 2 each).**

1. **Rural and regional development projects**: the building of roads, schools, health centres, water points and rural electrification, support to farmers (cotton, rice and livestock schemes, agricultural credit and inputs), irrigation projects, and the creation of agro-industries in the less developed regions.
2. **Decentralisation and the creation of growth poles**: the transfer of resources and powers to the regional and local councils, the creation of state universities and technical schools in the regions (for example in the Far North, the Adamawa and the North-West), and industrial incentives so that jobs are created outside Douala and Yaounde; measures for the displaced people (humanitarian aid, resettlement) and the improvement of security.

*Marks: (i) 6; (ii) 4.*

questions.enonce_markdown: c) Explain any THREE measures by the government to improve on transport development in Cameroon. (7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Any three measures, each explained (about 2 to 3 marks).**

1. **Construction, tarring and maintenance of roads**: the main highways (for example the Douala-Yaounde road and the corridors to Chad and the Central African Republic) and the feeder roads in the regions, with a road maintenance fund and road-maintenance brigades; this reduces transport costs and opens up the rural areas.
2. **Modernisation of ports and the railway**: the extension of the port of Douala, the new deep-sea port at Kribi, and the improvement of the railway (the concession to a private operator and the rehabilitation of the Douala-Yaounde-Ngaoundere line), which carry bulk goods and passengers over long distances.
3. **Airports and air transport**: the improvement of the international airports (Douala and Yaounde-Nsimalen) and of regional aerodromes (Garoua, Maroua, Bafoussam...), which speeds up the movement of people and goods.
4. **Bridges and urban transport**: new bridges (for example over the Wouri at Douala), urban road programmes, and public transport schemes to reduce congestion.
5. **Private sector participation and regional co-operation**: public-private partnerships, the liberalisation of transport, the creation of transport corridors with neighbouring countries and the road, rail and river projects within CEMAC.

*Marks: three measures, each explained.*
